evidence.quote: | NetEndOfMonth days -> DateOnly(issueDate.Year, issueDate.Month, DateTime.DaysInMonth(issueDate.Year, issueDate.Month)).AddDays days
| Some days when eom && days >= 1 && days <= 365 -> Ok(Some(NetEndOfMonth days))

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The new due-date rule is in `Summa.Ledger.Invoicing.dueDate`, which is Tier 1. The terms-field validation (1 to 365 days, EOM suffix) is in `Summa.Web.Engine`, which is Tier 2. The record format change is in `Summa.Storage`, also Tier 2. Tier 3 and Tier 4 code is untouched, so nothing re-derives the rule.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The change adds no clock, randomness, I/O or persistence call. The due-date calculation uses `DateTime.DaysInMonth`, which is a pure calendar function, and takes the issue date as an argument. The parser is pure and the storage codec only converts to and from JSON. The change touches no Tier 3 or Tier 4 code.

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The words for the new terms, `Net {days} EOM`, are written in two places: `Documents.termsText` and the audit-trail `Invoicing.termsWords`. The two texts agree, and the existing terms already had this duplication, so the change extends it. The due-date rule, the storage kind `net-eom` and the 1 to 365 bound each have one definition.

evidence.quote:
| DayOfNextMonth day ->
        let first = DateOnly(issueDate.Year, issueDate.Month, 1).AddMonths 1
| true, day when digits |> Seq.forall Char.IsAsciiDigit && day >= 1 && day <= 28 -> Ok(Some(DayOfNextMonth day))

ARC-REV-01.rationale: The due-date rule and the ordinal wording are in `Summa.Ledger` (Tier 1). The `day N` form validation (1 to 28) is in `Summa.Web.Engine` (Tier 2). Storage in `Summa.Storage` only encodes and decodes the value. Tier 3 and Tier 4 add nothing.

ARC-REV-02.rationale: The change adds no effect. `dueDate` and `ordinal` are pure functions, and the parser and codec are pure. The change touches no Tier 3 or Tier 4 code.

evidence.quote: | DayOfNextMonth day -> $"Due the {ordinal day} of next month"
| Some(DayOfNextMonth day) -> $"Due the {ordinal day} of next month"

ARC-REV-03.rationale: The phrase `Due the {ordinal day} of next month` is written in both `termsText` and `termsWords`. The two copies agree, and the change extends the existing duplication. `ordinal` is defined once and used by both. The error text was moved into a single `termsError` binding, which removes a copy. The 1 to 28 bound has a single definition, in the engine parser.
